STUDYQURAN:1:3/r7.claim: Mercy manifests in names of beauty and is veiled in names of rigor by the inseparability of kindness from majesty and divine determining power; God is compassionate to all and merciful to believers.
STUDYQURAN:1:3/r7.anchor: God is thus said to be Compassionate toward all of creation and Merciful toward the believers

STUDYQURAN:1:3/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:3/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:3/r8.claim: Placed between God’s sovereignty over space and mastery of time, this verse presents mercy as encompassing all time and space, as in 7:156.
STUDYQURAN:1:3/r8.anchor: this verse indicates that God’s Mercy encompasses and interpenetrates all time and all space, as in 7:156

TAB:1:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:3/r1.speaker: author
TAB:1:3/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī does not repeat the explanation of the two names because he has already explained them in the basmala commentary.
TAB:1:3/r1.anchor: قال أبو جعفر :  قد مضى البيان عن تأويل قوله «الرحمن الرحيم » ،   في تأويل «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم »

TAB:1:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:3/r2.speaker: author
TAB:1:3/r2.claim: He argues that the basmala is not a verse of the Fātiḥa: otherwise the same complete verse would occur twice in immediate succession without a separating passage.
TAB:1:3/r2.anchor: إذ لو كان ذلك كذلك لكان ذلك إعادة آية بمعنى واحد ولفظ واحد مرتين من غير فصل يفصل بينهما

TAB:1:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:3/r3.speaker: جماعة من أهل التأويل
TAB:1:3/r3.claim: Some exegetes say al-ḥamdu lillāh separates the repeated phrase only on the surface, since the intended order places al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm before Rabb al-ʿālamīn.
TAB:1:3/r3.anchor: وقالوا :  إن ذلك من الموخّر الذي معناه التقديم ،   وإنما هو :  الحمد لله الرحمن الرحيم رب العالمين

TAB:1:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:3/r4.speaker: جماعة من أهل التأويل
TAB:1:3/r4.claim: They place Malik yawm al-dīn beside Rabb al-ʿālamīn because both describe sovereignty, and place the mercy names beside other praise of God.
TAB:1:3/r4.anchor: إن قوله :  «ملك يوم الدين » تعليم من الله عبده أن يصفه بالمُلْك في قراءة من قرأ مَلِك

TAB:1:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:3/r5.speaker: author
TAB:1:3/r5.claim: He says Arabic often puts a phrase before the words it semantically modifies, citing Jarīr and Qur'an 18:1–2 to support the opposing word-order analysis while retaining his conclusion about the basmala.
TAB:1:3/r5.anchor: نظائر ذلك من التقديم الذي هو بمعنى التأخير والمؤخر الذي هو بمعنى التقديم في كلام العرب أفشى وفي منطقها أكثر من أن يحصى

TAB:1:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:3/r6.speaker: author
TAB:1:3/r6.claim: Jarīr's line and the wording of al-Kahf 18:1–2 illustrate this delayed-before order; he treats the examples as further evidence that the basmala is not a Fātiḥa verse.
TAB:1:3/r6.anchor: الحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الّذِي أَنْزَلَ على عَبْدِهِ الكتابَ وَلمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ عِوَجا قَيّما

TABATABAI:1:5#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:5#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:5#2/r1.claim: Divine mercy is analyzed as giving and effusion that remove need; Rahman is an intensive form for abundant, universal mercy, while Rahim indicates enduring mercy, fitting believers in particular.
TABATABAI:1:5#2/r1.anchor: إن الرحمن عام للمؤمن والكافر والرحيم خاص بالمؤمن

TABATABAI:1:1-5#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:1-5#6/r5.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:1:1-5#6/r5.claim: Al-Sadiq says Rahman extends to all creation, while Rahim is particular to believers; another formulation calls Rahman a special name with a general attribute and Rahim a general name with a special attribute.
TABATABAI:1:1-5#6/r5.anchor: الرحمن بجميع خلقه، الرحيم بالمؤمنين خاصة

TABATABAI:1:1-5#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:1-5#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:1-5#6/r6.claim: The author explains Rahman as universal creative effusion in this life and Rahim as mercy in both creation and religious guidance, whose lasting salvation is particular to believers.
TABATABAI:1:1-5#6/r6.anchor: الرحمن يختص بالإفاضة التكوينية التي يعم المؤمن والكافر

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.claim: The Prophet transmits God's division of al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: each phrase receives divine acknowledgement and a tailored promise of blessing, mercy, ease of judgment, reward, help, and fulfillment of the servant's requests.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.anchor: قسمت فاتحة الكتاب بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي، ولعبدي ما سأل

TABRISI:1:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:3/r1.speaker: علي بن عيسى الرماني
TABRISI:1:3/r1.claim: Al-Rummani says Rahman and Rahim are repeated for emphasis; there is no redundancy because the earlier basmala links servitude to gratitude and this verse links praise to the blessings meriting it.
TABRISI:1:3/r1.anchor: قد مضى تفسيرها وإنما أعاد الرحمن والرحيم للمبالغة وقال علي بن عيسى الرماني: في الأول ذكر العبودية

THALABI:v1p103/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p103/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p103/r4.claim: In the divine report dividing prayer between God and the servant, the basmala glorifies God, al-ḥamdu praises Him, al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm extols Him, Mālik delegates the matter, the worship-and-help verse is shared, and guidance is granted to the servant.
THALABI:v1p103/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «يقول الله: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبادي نصفين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r1.claim: Divine mercy means God's willing good and blessing for its recipients and is an essential attribute; human mercy is tenderness and compassion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r1.anchor: معنى الرحمة في صفة الله تعالى: إرادته الخير والنعمة بأهله، وهي صفة ذات،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r2.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās explains pairing al-Raḥmān with al-Raḥīm by treating the first as Hebrew and the second as Arabic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r2.anchor: سألت أبا العباس (¬6) لم جمع بين الرحمن والرحيم؟ فقال: لأن الرحمن عبراني فأتى معه الرحيم العربي،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r3.claim: An objection cites pre-Islamic poetry using al-Raḥmān to argue that Arabs knew the name before Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r3.anchor: ألا ضربت تلك الفتاة (¬4) هجينها ... ألا قضب الرحمن ربي يمينها (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r4.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās replies that most pre-Islamic Arabs did not know the name; Quraysh said they knew al-Raḥmān only as a man in al-Yamāma, and a few poets learned it from scriptural communities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r4.anchor: فقال (¬6): إن جمهور العرب كانوا لا يعرفون "الرحمن" في الجاهلية،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r5.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r5.claim: His intended distinction is that al-Raḥmān circulated across Hebrew and Arabic speech, while al-Raḥīm was distinctively Arabic and so clarified the pairing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r5.anchor: ومراد أبي العباس أن الرحمن يتكلم به بالعبرانية (¬7)، وتتكلم به العرب،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r6.claim: The author instead holds that al-Raḥmān is an Arabic name derived from mercy, supported by Arabic patterns such as laḥfān, nadmān, and ghaḍbān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r6.anchor: والصحيح أنه مشتق من الرحمة، وأنه اسم عربي لوجود هذا البناء في كلامهم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r7.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r7.claim: Al-Layth treats al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm as two names both derived from mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r7.anchor: قال الليث: {الرحمن الرحيم} اسمان، اشتقاقهما (¬3) من الرحمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats the two words as divine attributes meaning possessor of mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هما صفتان لله تعالى، معناهما ذو الرحمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r9.claim: The question What is al-Raḥmān? in 25:60 asks about the attribute, not the person's identity, so it does not prove the name was unknown; it may also express irreverence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r9.anchor: فهو سؤال عن الصفة، ولذلك قالوا: {وما الرحمن}، ولم يقولوا: ومن، والقوم جهلوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r10.claim: Some scholars say al-Raḥmān is more emphatic than al-Raḥīm, like ʿallām compared with ʿalīm; they call the former mercy for this world and the latter mercy for the afterlife.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p455/r10.anchor: واختلفوا في أن أي الاسمين من هذين أشد مبالغة، فقال قوم: الرحمن أشد مبالغة من الرحيم،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r4.claim: The two divine attributes mean possessing mercy, an abiding divine quality understood as willing good; the names do not differ in meaning, like nadmān and nadīm.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r4.anchor: وهي إرادة الخير، ولا فرق بينهما، مثل: ندمان ونديم.

ELMALILI:1:3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r1.claim: Human mercy begins as an affective tenderness toward the afflicted and aims to remove harm and establish good; sometimes a word or gesture suffices, while its complete end is voluntary beneficence.
ELMALILI:1:3/r1.anchor: bir iyilik duygusudur demiştik, ki bu ibtidâ şefkat gibi teessür ve infi‘âl kabîlinden bir meyl-i nefsânî olarak başlar

ELMALILI:1:3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r2.claim: In ordinary speech, calling someone merciful usually means tender-hearted capacity, while calling them very merciful points to visible beneficial action.
ELMALILI:1:3/r2.anchor: ekseriyâ “rikkat-i kalb” dediğimiz hâlet-i rûhiyeyi, kābiliyyet-i infi‘âliyeyi kastederiz, fakat “pek merhametli, çok merhametli” dediğimiz zaman da netîce-i fi‘liyesinin zuhûrunu anlarız

ELMALILI:1:3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r3.claim: Because God is beyond change and affect, divine mercy cannot be explained as the same psychological state as human compassion; both rational and revealed indications support this.
ELMALILI:1:3/r3.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah ise ‘alâim-i hudûs olan tegayyür ve infi‘alden

ELMALILI:1:3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r4.speaker: müfessirîn
ELMALILI:1:3/r4.claim: Exegetes allow some lexical metaphor in divine mercy: either its necessary result, deliverance and beneficence, or the prior will of good that causes beneficence.
ELMALILI:1:3/r4.anchor: müfessirîn burada az çok bir mecâz-ı lügavî bulunduğunu söylerler ki bu da iki suretle mülâhaza edilir

ELMALILI:1:3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r5.claim: On the first interpretation mercy is an attribute of action; on the second, the will of good is an essential attribute, since willing is choice rather than affect.
ELMALILI:1:3/r5.anchor: evvelkine göre rahmet sıfat-ı fiilden, ikinciye göre sıfat-ı zâtiyeden olur

ELMALILI:1:3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r6.claim: Since divine mercy is perfect and both adjectives occur, he prefers including both the essential will of good and its acts of beneficence.
ELMALILI:1:3/r6.anchor: burada iki mânayı da kastetmek daha muvâfıktır

ELMALILI:1:3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r7.claim: He explains Rahmân as a special, stable adjective for God's essential will of good, and Rahîm as an intensive active participle for its manifested beneficence; some reverse this mapping.
ELMALILI:1:3/r7.anchor: “Rahmân” sıfat-ı hâssa olduğuna nazaran garîze ve sübut ifade eden sıfat-ı müşebbehe olarak irâde-i hayr sıfat-ı zâtiyesi, “Rahîm” de mübalağa ile ism-i fâil

ELMALILI:1:3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r8.speaker: Bunu aks edenler
ELMALILI:1:3/r8.claim: Some interpreters reverse the allocation of essential and active meanings between Rahmân and Rahîm.

ELMALILI:1:3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r9.claim: His preferred account treats divine names and attributes as literally true, not metaphorical, while recognizing that their divine meanings are not identical to human ones.
ELMALILI:1:3/r9.anchor: bizim muhtârımız şudur ki sıfât ve esmâ-i ilâhiye mânalarında mecaz değil, hakikattirler

ELMALILI:1:3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r10.claim: Divine knowledge and will are eternal creator-attributes and the source of human counterparts; human acquisition, desire, and temporal change are incidental conditions, not their essence.
ELMALILI:1:3/r10.anchor: İlm-i ilâhî ve irâde-i ilâhiye ise bizim bu sıfatlarımızın

ELMALILI:1:3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r11.claim: He distinguishes divine rahmet from human merhamet in Turkish, so translating Rahmân Rahîm simply as “very compassionate” is inadequate.

ELMALILI:1:3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3/r12.claim: A fuller explanation is boundless mercy and beneficent outpouring, combining the essential will of good with rescue from harm and delivery to blessings.
ELMALILI:1:3/r12.anchor: nâmütenâhî rahmet sâhibi, nâmütenâhî feyz-i in‘âm, hayr u ihsan saçıcı” diye bir îzah yapabiliriz

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r1.claim: Harm is rooted in nonexistence and its causes, good in existence and its causes; pains warn of lost good, while pleasures announce a share in existence.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r1.anchor: âfâtın hakikati ‘adem ve sevâik-i ‘ademdir, hayrâtın hakikati de vücûd ve sevâik-i vücûddur

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r2.claim: Despair of God and His mercy is the root of suffering, while faith in God and His mercy is the root of pleasure and hope.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r2.anchor: Bunların başı Hak’tan ve rahmet-i Hak’tan yeistir. Ni‘am ve hayrât ile alâkadar olan bütün lezzetlerimiz

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r3.claim: Worldly life is a renewed struggle between nonbeing and being, pain and pleasure, despair and faith, sustained by divine mercy and human effort; the afterlife eternally separates their outcomes.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r3.anchor: Hayât-ı dünyâ böyle ‘adem ile vücûdun, âlâm ile lezâizin, yeis ile imanın, rahmet-i Rahmân ve sa‘y u te‘âvün ile yenilen bir mücadelesi şeklidir

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r4.claim: Human good begins with being brought from nonexistence and culminates in passing from the finite to the infinite.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r4.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bizim hayr ve lezâizimizin başlangıcı ‘ademden vücûda

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r5.claim: Rahmân's mercy is God's will to bring every possible thing from nonexistence into existence, because existence is the source of every good and blessing.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r5.anchor: Rahmet-i rahmâniye bütün mümkinâtın ‘ademden vücûda ihrâcını ifade eden irâde-i vücûd ve in‘âm-ı vücûd olduğundan

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r6.claim: Rahmân creates human bodily and spiritual existence and supplies the provisions that sustain life; no creature falls outside this encompassing mercy.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r6.anchor: bizi cismâniyet ve rûhâniyetimizle ‘ademden vücûda getirerek halk eden ve bununla beraber esbâb-ı bekā ve hayâtımız olan nimetleri de ihzar ve îsâl eyleyen

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r7.claim: The full scope of Rahmân's mercy includes creating beings who can reason and act by choice.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r7.anchor: âkil ve bi’l-ihtiyâr fâil olacak mevcûdât halk eylemek de rahmet-i rahmâniyenin kemâl-i şümûlü muktezâsındandır

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r8.claim: Multiple independent wills would introduce an accidental plurality that undermines lasting existence, since God's partner is intrinsically false and nonexistent.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r8.anchor: iradelerin ta‘addüdü hasebiyle vücûdda bir nevi şirk-i ‘arazî zuhur eder. Hâlbuki şirk ile vücûd ve devâm-ı vücûd mümteni‘dir

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r9.claim: Natural and moral evils ultimately grow from multiplicity and claims of partnership, because divine unity is necessary for existence.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r9.anchor: âlemde gerek tabîî ve gerek ahlâkī ne kadar şürûr tasavvur edilirse hepsinin kökü ta‘addüd ve da‘vâ-yı şirktir

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r10.claim: Rahîm's mercy preserves balance by governing the many free wills through one divine will, sustaining existence while allowing choice.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r10.anchor: bütün tecelliyât-ı vücûdu bir irade ile idare ve idâme etmek öyle dakīk bir nimet ve öyle ebedî bir hayırdır

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r11.claim: Perfect divine nurture balances necessity with choice; philosophers call this delicate reconciliation the riddle of existence.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r11.anchor: Kemâl-i terbiye îcab ile ihtiyârın işte bu ihtilâtındaki muvâzenede ve kemâl-i rabbânî felâsifenin “mu‘ammâ-yı vücûd” dedikleri bu mu‘âdele-i rahîmiyededir

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r12.speaker: eslâf-ı müfessirîn
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r12.claim: Earlier exegetes call Rahîm's mercy the subtleties of blessings and also interpret it by the blessings of the afterlife.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r12.anchor: eslâf-ı müfessirîn rahmet-i rahîmiyeye “dekāik-i ni‘am” tâbir etmişler ve gaye itibariyle da ni‘am-ı uhreviye ile tefsir etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r13.claim: God gives each person a share of choice, then judges acquired rights on the true balance and assigns reward or punishment for even an atom's worth; punishment safeguards reward, whose primary aim is mercy.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r13.anchor: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًۭا يَرَهُۥ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍۢ شَرًّۭا يَرَهُۥ

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r14.claim: Initial existence under Rahmân keeps creatures on their course; a second existence under Rahîm concerns free agents, some of whom depart from duty and upset the balance through choice.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r14.anchor: Rahmet-i rahmâniye içindeki vücûd-i ibtidâîde hiçbir mevcud yolundan inhiraf etmez. Rahmet-i rahîmiye içindeki vücûd-i sânî ise ashâb-ı irâdeye ait olduğundan

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r15.claim: God's own Rahmânic will remains sovereign over the general balance of justice and mercy.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r15.anchor: bu mu‘âdelenin mîzân-ı umûmîsinde de lâ-şerîke leh olan Hak teâlâ’nın

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r16.claim: The verse about the Merciful established over the Throne illustrates this encompassing divine governance.

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r17.claim: Rahmân gives existence and its sustaining blessings to all rational beings whether or not they seek them; Rahîm addresses their voluntary striving and offers greater, desired gifts by God's will.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r17.anchor: er-Rahmân diyor ki: Ey zevi’l-‘ukūl! Siz isteseniz de istemeseniz de

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r18.claim: Rational beings are created to reflect divine mercy through their own will, draw near to God, and attain the greatest favor; they remain accountable for choices that threaten shared existence.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r18.anchor: Ey zevi’l-‘ukūl! Ey ashâb-ı irâde! Siz diğerleri gibi değilsiniz, onlar sade irâde-i rahmâniyenin ceberûtuna mahkumdurlar

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r19.claim: God calls people away from denial and associationism toward loving, upright work for truth, justice, mercy, and eternal reward.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r19.anchor: Haydi Hakk’ı inkâr etmeyiniz, şirk koşmayınız, Hakk’a kurbiyet ve hatta niyâbet için hak ve irâde-i hak yolunda mahabbetle

ELMALILI:1:3#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r20.claim: Divine lordship is not merely coercive destruction: it increases blessings through mercy; the cited verse promises good and more to those who do good.
ELMALILI:1:3#2/r20.anchor: Benim rubûbiyetim kahr u ceberûttan ibaret bir tasarruf-ı tazyîk ve i‘dâm değil, böyle rahmâniyet ve rahîmiyet ile tezyîd-i in‘âm eden bir rubûbiyet-i celîle ve cemîledir

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r1.claim: He raises and rejects the thought that after creating free agents, God delegated future outcomes to them and withdrew, leaving them masters of reward, punishment, and the future.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r1.anchor: Acaba Rabbü’l-âlemin ashâb-ı irâdeyi halk ettikten sonra istikbalin mukadderâtını onlara tefvîz etmiş ve kendisi acaba hicâb-ı izzete çekilmiş değil midir

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r2.claim: This conceit mistakes limited present choice for absolute creative power and unrestricted freedom, a claim of partnership that underlies human calamity and injustice.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r2.anchor: irâde-i cüz’iyeye mutlak bir irâde-i külliye ve her kayıttan âzâde bir ihtiyar ve bir kudret-i hâlıka kıymeti isnad ederek kendilerini kādir-i kül

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r3.claim: Without divine justice and mercy regulating this arrogance, human society would destroy itself; the verse links corruption on land and sea to people's deeds.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r3.anchor: rahmet-i ilâhiyenin bunun üzerindeki ta‘dîlâtı, inzibâtı olmasa cem‘iyyet-i beşeriye üç gün içinde birbirini yer bitirir

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r4.claim: New creation continually occurs beyond human will; paralysis can instantly humble the strongest, and the preserved mummies of Pharaohs show that past rulers no longer own their former might.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r4.anchor: Hâlbuki âlemde ve hele hayatta her an irâde-i beşerden hâriç halk-ı cedîd cereyan etmekte olduğu cihetle kuvveti kendisinin zanneden o kavî pazuları bir an içinde

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r5.claim: God holds the reins of existence and life in past and future alike: He is both First and Last, while the first agent and ultimate end are truly one.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r5.anchor: ve O’nun milkidir. O zannedildiği gibi sadece Evvel değil, hem Evvel ve hem Âhir’dir.

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r6.claim: The spherical bodies and cycles of time suggest this unity through their center and circumference.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r6.anchor: ecrâmın küriyyeti, zamanın istidâresi merkez ve muhîtinden bize bunu iş‘âr eder

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r7.claim: Some who sense God's control extend compulsion even to the present; human beings alternately boast “all me” in strength and appeal to another in weakness.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r7.anchor: Bu noktayı hissedenlerin bir kısmı mâzî ve istikbal şöyle d ursun, hâlde bile cebr-i mahza kāil olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r8.claim: The truth is neither pure determinism nor pure autonomy, but a middle position between the two.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r8.anchor: hakikat ise ne öyle ne böyledir, أَمْر بَيْنَ أَمْرَيْن’dir

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r9.claim: Human life combines body and spirit, reason and heart, capacity and action, necessity and choice; humans are neither absolutely compelled nor absolutely self-acting.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r9.anchor: Beşeriyet cisim ile rûhun, akıl ile kalbin, kābiliyet ile fâiliyetin, ıztırar ile ihtiyârın muhassalasıdır

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r10.claim: Both strict determinists and advocates of complete creative freedom fail to fit the evident balance of reality.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r10.anchor: müdde‘îlerinin ihtiyâr-ı hâlikāne dâvaları, hiçbir zaman mîzân-ı hakīkatin bedâhetiyle karşılaşamazlar

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r11.claim: Necessity in humans witnesses God's power, while their capacity to choose witnesses God's will; humans are brought into existence by God yet may choose their striving through divine mercy.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r11.anchor: Beşerde cihet-i ıztırar kudretullâhın şâhidi, cihet-i ihtiyar da irâdetullâhın şâhididir

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r12.claim: A person's present authority is a temporary, limited, borrowed trust and delegated commission from God, neither to be denied nor mistaken for an unremovable absolute title.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r12.anchor: müsâ‘ade-i Hakk’a mazhar bir salâhiyet-i niyâbiyeyi

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r13.claim: People receive future reward and punishment rather than distribute it; when their borrowed means are withdrawn, they receive as needy dependents, not owners.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r13.anchor: İnsan istikbaldeki mükâfat ve mücâzâtı verecek değil, alacaktır.

ELMALILI:1:3#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r14.claim: Absolute ownership of the heavens, earth, times, beings, matter, forces, capacities, and actions belongs to God as creator and sustainer.
ELMALILI:1:3#3/r14.anchor: bütün âlemînin mâliki, mübdi‘i, hâlıkı, mürebbîsi olan Allah teâlâ’nın milk-i mutlakıdır

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:3:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:3:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:3:kommentar/r1.claim: Because some rites recite the Fātiḥa without the Basmala, al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm here is an emphatic introduction of a new title, not a repetition.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:3:kommentar/r1.anchor: Da V. 1 nicht Teil des Textes ist – die Fātiḥa wird in einigen Riten bis heute ohne die Basmala rezitiert

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:3/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:3/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:3/r1.claim: For the meanings of Rahman and Rahim, the commentary directs readers back to its explanation of the basmala in 1:1.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:3/r1.anchor: Rahmân ve rahîm isimlerinin anlamları için 1.ayetin (Besmele) açıklamasına bakılabilir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r1.claim: Most authorities say the Opening was revealed in Mecca and was among the Qur'an's earliest revelations.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r1.anchor: اختلفوا فيها فعند الأكثرين هي مكية من أوائل ما نزل من القرآن

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r2.speaker: أبو ميسرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r2.claim: Abu Maysara reports that before revelation the Prophet fled when a caller addressed him; Waraqa advised him to stay and listen, after which the call instructed him to attest to God's oneness and Muhammad's messengerhood and recite the Opening.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r2.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا برز سمع مناديا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r3.claim: Ali reports that the Opening descended in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام قال: نزلت فاتحة الكتاب بمكة من كنز تحت العرش

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet recited the basmala and the Opening in Mecca, Quraysh responded with a curse or similar insult.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قام النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بمكة فقال: {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين}

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r5.claim: Mujahid alone says the Opening is Medinan; al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl calls this an isolated slip against the scholarly majority.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r5.anchor: وعند مجاهد أن الفاتحة مدنية. قال الحسين بن الفضل: لكل عالم هفوة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r6.speaker: الواحدي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi argues it must be Meccan because the Meccan Hijr 15:87 calls the seven oft-repeated a gift to the Prophet; it is unreasonable to say he prayed for over a decade without the Opening.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r6.anchor: ومما يقطع به على أنها مكية قوله تعالى: {ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني والقرآن العظيم} يعني: الفاتحة.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after Ubayy recited the Opening, the Prophet said no comparable surah was revealed in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an, calling it the seven oft-repeated and mighty Qur'an given to him.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p19/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وقرأ عليه أبي بن كعب أم القرآن، فقال:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r3.claim: Rahman is the fa'lan form, suggesting renewed occurrence and fullness of mercy; al-Tafsir al-Qayyim compares it to being filled with anger or regret.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r3.anchor: جاء في (التفسير القيم) : "ألا ترى أنهم يقولون غضبان، للممتلىء غضباً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p34/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p34/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p34/r1.claim: Rahim's fa'il form marks a stable quality, so pairing Rahman and Rahim conveys mercy as both renewed and lasting; either form alone could suggest impermanence or a merely fixed quality.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p34/r1.anchor: فجاء بالوصفين للدلالة على أن صفته الثابتة والمتجددة، هي الرحمة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p34/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p34/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p34/r2.claim: Mercy after Rabb reassures worshippers and signals that every aspect of lordship should be merciful; God describes His exemplary messenger as kind and merciful to believers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p34/r2.anchor: وفيه إشارةٌ إلى أن المربي ينبغي أن يتحلى بالرحمة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p40/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p40/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p40/r1.claim: God is praiseworthy in His essence, lordship, rightly placed mercy, and ownership of Judgment Day; the sequence spans all times from eternity through the endless afterlife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p40/r1.anchor: وقد استغرق هذا الحمد الأزمنة كلها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r1.claim: The praise covers time from eternity to eternity, echoed by praise in the first and last life and at the end of judgment; this fullness makes al-Fatiha worthy to be the Mother of the Book.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r1.anchor: فاستغرق الحمد الزمان كلَّه من الأزل إلى الأبد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r2.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r2.claim: The names following praise show God is praiseworthy in divinity, lordship, mercy, and kingship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p41/r2.anchor: جاء في (التفسير القيم) : "في ذِكْرِ هذه الأسماء بعد الحمد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r4.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r4.claim: The Merciful and Compassionate names express the one God’s complete mercy, generosity, favor, and beneficence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r4.anchor: أما قوله: {الرحمان الرحيم} فيدل على أن الإله الواحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r6.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r6.claim: Al-Razi summarizes praise as God’s existence and choice, lordship as unity, mercy as compassion in both worlds, and Judgment Day as wisdom and mercy.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p72/r6.anchor: وقوله: {الرحمان الرحيم} يدل على رحمته في الدنيا والآخرة.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p16/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p16/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p16/r1.claim: In Arabic morphology, fa'lan (as in Rahman) suggests fullness and a renewed, occurring state, while fa'il (Rahim) suggests a stable quality; examples include غضبان/عطشان and طويل/ضعيف.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p16/r1.anchor: الصفة فعلان تمثل الحدوث والتجدد والامتلاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p16/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p16/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p16/r2.claim: Combining Rahman and Rahim presents mercy as both renewed and permanently established, preventing either name alone from suggesting that mercy may lapse.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p16/r2.anchor: جاء سبحانه بالصفتين مجتمعتين ليدل على أن صفاته الثابتة والمتجددة هي الرحمة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p17/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p17/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p17/r1.claim: Rahman comes first to stress immediate, renewed, abundant mercy for people who favor what arrives soon, as 75:20 observes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p17/r1.anchor: لأن الإنسان في طبيعته عجول وكثيراً ما يؤثر الإنسان الشيء الآتي السريع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p17/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p17/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p17/r2.claim: Rahim after Rabb signals that mercy should mark a true educator, master, and caretaker; God also described His Messenger as merciful.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p17/r2.anchor: ووقوع كلمة " الرحيم " بعد كلمة الرب يدلنا على أن الرحمة هي من صفات الله تعالى العليا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p18/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p18/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p18/r4.claim: The sequence praises God for His essence, lordship, properly placed mercy, and ownership and kingship on the day of recompense.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p18/r4.anchor: محمود في رحمته يضعها حيث يجب أن توضع وهو محمود يوم الدين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r1.claim: The opening attributes span all time: praise before creation, at creation, through continuing mercy, and through the unending recompense of the afterlife, as 28:70 says.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p19/r1.anchor: استغرق الحمد كل الأزمنة من الأزل إلى الأبد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.claim: The guidance request ties the chapter together: Rabb guides, Rahman and Rahim show mercy, worship and reliance require the path, and the favored oppose the astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.anchor: هذا الدعاء ارتبط بأول السورة وبوسطها وآخرها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r1.claim: After stating God's universal nurturing, the verse declares His immense mercy; the majority read both names in the genitive, while Zayd, Abu al-ʿAliya, Ibn al-Sumayqa, and ʿIsa ibn ʿAmr read them accusatively, and several others raise them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r1.anchor: والجمهور على خفضهما ونصبهما زيد وأبو العالية وإبن السميقع وعيسى بن عمرو

ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r2.speaker: بعض ساداتنا
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r2.claim: Some Sufi masters infer from repeating the two names here and in the basmala that the basmala is not a verse of the Fatiha; al-Alusi calls the inference weak because each occurrence has a distinct purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r2.anchor: وأستدل بعض ساداتنا بتكرارهما على أن البسملة ليست آية من الفاتحة وليس بالقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r3.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r3.claim: Al-Razi explains the repetition as stressing mercy more than other matters, then balancing hope with the warning that God is Master of Judgment Day; al-Alusi objects that divinity is repeated too.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r3.anchor: قال الإمام الرازي قدس سره في بيان حكمة التكرار التقدير كأنه قيل له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r4.claim: Al-Alusi's Sufi reading makes Rahman and Rahim a detailed account of Rabb's general nurturing: care may be mediated or immediate, and mediated care may involve hardship or pure kindness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r4.anchor: وعندي بمسلك صوفي أن ذكر الرحمن الرحيم تفصيل من وجه لما في رب العالمين من الإجمال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r5.claim: Rahman points to nurturing through intermediaries and across the worlds, including mercy mixed with painful medicine; Rahim points to direct nurturing through divine words as pure blessing for the fully happy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p82/r5.anchor: فالرحمن يشير إلى التربية بالوسائط وغيرها في عالمه والرحيم يشير إلى التربية بلا واسطة في كلماته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r5.claim: The descriptions close by pointing to resurrection, just as Lord of the worlds opened with origination; they explain the prior praise and prepare for the prayer that follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r5.anchor: وإنما ختم سبحانه هذه الأوصاف بهذا الوصف إشارة إلى الإعادة كما أفتتح بما يشير إلى الإبداء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r6.claim: The five names answer four grounds for praising someone: inherent perfection, past beneficence, hoped-for future kindness, and fear of power; God encompasses them all.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r6.anchor: أن الذي يحمده الناس ويعظمونه إنما يكون حمده وتعظيمه لأحد أمور أربعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r7.claim: An argument for rational gratitude before revelation says the verse establishes God's praiseworthiness through creation, mercy, and future judgment; al-Alusi replies that this proof itself is scriptural, not rational.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r7.anchor: ومن الناس من أستدل كما قال الإمام على وجوب اشكر عقلا قبل مجيء الشرع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r8.claim: Al-Alusi says deriving the duty of gratitude from God's own revealed declaration only proves it through revelation, so it cannot establish a pre-revelation rational duty.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r8.anchor: فهو سمعي لا عقلي فالمستدل به كناطح صخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r9.claim: A Sufi anthropology maps the five divine names to the human's angelic intellect, devilish, predatory, animal, and dense bodily dimensions, with cited verses illustrating the correspondences.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p85/r9.anchor: فالإنسان بدن ونفس شيطانية ونفس سبعية ونفس بهيمية وجوهر ملكي عقلي

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:3/r1.claim: The repetition of الرحمن الرحيم supplies a causal explanation, which the commentary will explain later.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.speaker: أبو الفضل محمد المشدالي المغربي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.claim: Al-Mashdali's method for Qur'anic coherence is to identify a surah's purpose, its prerequisites and their distance from the goal, then answer expectations raised as the discourse unfolds.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.anchor: قال شيخنا الإمام المحقق أبو الفضل محمد بن العلامة القدوة أبي عبد الله محمد ابن العلامة القدوة أبي القاسم محمد المشدالي المغربي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.claim: A surah's name summarizes its purpose, as a title signals the details within; Adam demonstrated this naming principle when he named things before the angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.anchor: أن اسم كل سورة مترجم عن مقصودها هلأن أسم كل شيء تظهر المناسبة بينه وبين مسماه عنوانه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.claim: The Fatiha's many titles converge on مراقبة: it is the Mother of the Book, foundation, oft-repeated, treasure, healing, sufficing, complete, protecting, incantation, praise, thanks, supplication and prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.anchor: فمدار هذه الأسماء كما ترى على أمر خفي كاف لكل مراد وهو المراقبة التي سأقول إنها مقصودها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.claim: The Fatiha is a treasure, cure, sufficiency, fulfillment, protection and incantation; it gathers praise, gratitude and supplication, with prayer as their greatest assembly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.anchor: فكل شيء لا يفتتح بها لا اعتداد به ، وهي كنز لكل شيء شافية لكل داء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.claim: The Fatiha's purpose is to establish God's exclusive right to all praise and perfection, sovereignty over both worlds, worship and aid, and to ask for the path of the successful rather than the doomed; its center is مراقبة.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.anchor: الغرض الذي سبقت له الفاتحة وه إثبات استحقاق الله تعالى لجميع المحامد وصفا الكمال ، واختصاصه بملك الدنيا والآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.claim: The basmala relates to the Fatiha as the Fatiha relates to the Qur'an: each is a compact synthesis of what the larger whole details.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.anchor: وأشد منه أنه لما كانت نسبة البسملة من الفاتحة نسبة الفاتحة من القرآن صدرت بها الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r3.claim: Allah is a proper name encompassing all beautiful names; Rahman precedes Rahim because it is exclusive and more emphatic, following the order of existence, general mercy, then worship-specific mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r3.anchor: ولما كان اسم الجلالة علما وكان جامعا لجميع معاني الأسماء الحسنى أولية الرحمن من حيث أنه كالعلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r4.claim: The repeated mercy names affirm that God deserves these attributes intrinsically, fit His lordship and sovereignty, and show mercy prevailing over wrath; universal mercy also excludes every defect.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r4.anchor: وكررهما بعهد تنبيها عل وجوب ذلك للربوبية والملك وللدلالة على أن الرحمة غلبت الغضب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r9.claim: Lordship does not yield wellbeing without mercy, so Rahman and Rahim follow al-hamd and encourage people to persist in praising God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r9.anchor: ولما كانت مرتبة الربوبية لا تستجمع الصلاح إل بالرحمة اتبع ذلك بصفتي { الرحمن الرحيم } ترغبيا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p14/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p14/r1.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p14/r1.claim: Al-Ghazali's principle that the Qur'an contains no repetition prompts a further explanation for repeating Rahman and Rahim.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p14/r1.anchor: عن الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي رحمه الله تعالى أنه لا مكرر في القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.claim: Al-Harali says all Qur'an is God's speech, but some verses voice what creatures at different levels ought to say yet cannot express; God teaches them words that fulfill their duty.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أى هذه وما بهدها مما جاء كلام الله فيه جارياعلى لسان خلقه فإن القرآن كله كلام الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.claim: Al-Harali explains the sound report that God divided prayer between Himself and His servant: the first three verses are God's praise, which He accepts from the reciting servant as praise and glorification.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.anchor: وتلك هي صلاتهم المقسمة التى عبر عنها فيما صح عنه علية الصلاة والسلام من قوله تعالى : ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.claim: The Qur'an's arrangement is miraculous, so the Fatiha must retain its required order in prayer; rearrangement or insertion of foreign material invalidates it. Al-Isfahani locates its clearest inimitability in order.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : فإن القرآن معجز والركن الأبين الإعجاز يتعلق بالنظم والترتيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.speaker: مسعود التفتازاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.claim: Al-Taftazani maps the Fatiha's blessings to two creations and two preservations: creation in Rabb al-alamin, preservation in mercy, second creation in judgment, and afterlife preservation in worship onward.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.anchor: كما قال العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي . إلى جميع النعم فغنها ترجع إلى إيجاد وإبقاء ثانيافي دار الفناء والبقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.claim: Al-Harali says the seven repeated verses are the Qur'an's gathered essence and its contents will be disclosed at creation's completion; earlier scriptures progress from changeable scrolls and lasting books to the Qur'an, which completes religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في مفتاح الباب القفل لفهم القرآن المنزل في أخر الباب التاسع منه : ولننه هذه الأبواب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.claim: Al-Harali contrasts the Qur'an's detailed, dispersed sequence with the Fatiha's seven complete universals, and makes the Fatiha a mirror of the servant's move from misguidance to guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.anchor: ووجه فوت أم القرآن مقصود تنزيله التفصيل والجوامع , فيه نجوم مبثوثة غير منتظمة , وحداة إثر واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.claim: A Prophetic report says he was sent to complete noble character; the author links this completion with the Fatiha's comprehensive opening and the Qur'an's culmination.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.anchor: بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق . أن إلى ربك المنتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.claim: Al-Harali describes the Qur'an's majesty through rulings spanning immediate and deferred realities, witnessed experience, and reports of the past and patterns that recur in time.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.anchor: ومن مجيده وهو ما حربت أحكامه من بين عاجل ما شهد وآجل ما علم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes gradual descent that moves understanding between states and rulings from descent from high to low, which may occur with or without intermediaries.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.anchor: وما كان منه بتدريج وتقريب للأفهام ففاءت من حال إلى حال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.claim: The passage names al-Baqara 2:281 as the last revealed verse and says its recitation position between the debt verse and the verse before it shows revelation and recitation order can differ.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.anchor: وجعلوها بين آية الدين والآية قبلها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an's sevenfold gathering in Muhammad's heart relates to the Mother of Qur'an's universals as the Qur'an's gathering in his heart relates to the Mother.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.anchor: وأما الجمع ففي قلبه نسبة جوامعه السبع في أم القرآن إلى القرآن بمنزلة نسبة جمعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an reached the Prophet on his tongue over the span of the prophetic mission, after its descent to the lowest heaven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.anchor: وعلى لسانه في أمد أيام النبوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.claim: Aisha reports that Muhammad's character was the Qur'an, making his conduct the visible form of its inner reality.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.anchor: قالت عائشة رضى الله عنها : كان خلقه القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.claim: Al-Harali says the Fatiha is the Qur'an's mother: its first three verses encompass the divine names and attributes, while its last three cover the creature's way to God, mercy or failure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.anchor: فالآيات الثلاث الول قال شاملة لكل معنى تضمنته الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.claim: Recitation order can differ from revelation chronology; the verse allowing the Prophet to marry certain women was placed before a later restriction.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.anchor: فقد يتطابق قرآن الأمر وتطور الخلق وقد لا يتابق والله يتولى إقامتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.claim: In the authentic report in Muslim and the four Sunan, God says the Fatiha is divided between Himself and His servant: He answers praise, glorification and worship, and grants the servant's final requests.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضى الله عنه قال : سمعت زسول الله صلى اله عليه وسلم يقول

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.claim: Al-Baqara aims to prove the Book is guidance to follow; belief in the unseen, especially resurrection and the afterlife, is its greatest guidance and organizing theme.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.anchor: مقصودها إقامة الدليل على أن الكتاب هدى ليتبع يفي كل ما قال ، وأعظم ما يهدي إليه الإيمالن بالغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.claim: The cow story makes the surah's title apt because resurrection occurs through an apparently slight human cause; it is a clearer sign of divine power than Abraham's story or earlier Israelite resurrections.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.anchor: فلذلك سميت بها السورة وكانت بذلك أحق من قصة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنها في نوع البشر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.claim: The following comparison of hearts and stones shows the guided and astray: hearts become hard and wretched, while stones display fear and yield benefit that reaches God's servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.anchor: ولا سيما وقد اتبعت بوصف القلوب والحجارة بما عم اللمهتدين بالكتاب والضالين فوصفها بالقسوة الموجبة للشقوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.claim: The Book functions like a caliph from the resolute messengers, guiding every matter to the right exit: rejecting it fails, hesitation nearly perishes, and accepting it brings piety and excellence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.anchor: وفيها إشارة إلى أن هذا الكتاب فينا كما لو كان فينا خليفة من أولي العزم من الرسل يرشدنا في كل أمر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.claim: Al-Baqara is also called the Radiant and the Hump: it illuminates guidance and sufficiency, brightens believers' faces at judgment, and exalts belief in the afterlife above every other good after monotheism.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.anchor: وسميت الزهراء لإنارتها طريق الهداية والكفاية في الدنيا والآخرة ، ولأيجابها إسفار الوجوه يفي يوم الجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.claim: Because praise is the seventh inclusive letter, the Fatiha begins with it and gathers the seven universals diffused through the Qur'an, as the Qur'an gathers earlier scriptures.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.anchor: ولما كان حرف الحمد هو سابعها الجامع افتتح الله به سبحانه وتعالى الفاتحة أم القرآن وأم الكتاب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r3.claim: Alternatively, and the author says this is likelier, Rahmaniyyah universally grants blessings and removes harms whether for felicity or misery, while Rahimiyyah specifically gives the blessings and protection that lead to felicity.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r3.anchor: وأما الرحيمية فطهرتهم من مضار أبدانهم ورجاسة نفوسهم ومجهلة قلوبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.claim: Baqara answers the Fatiha's plea for guidance by directing worshippers to the Book, describing the guided and denied groups as patterns to follow or avoid; its pious are the straight path and its others the path of ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو أنه لما أخبلا سبحانه وتعالى أن عباده المخلصين سألوا في الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.claim: Alternatively, the surah's purpose is solely to describe the Book; it establishes the truth of its meaning, exposes disbelief and hypocrisy to show that inward faith matters, then proves its inimitable form and authority for teaching law.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.anchor: وإن شئت قلت : مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك فتوابع ولوازم

DURR-FULL:v1p24/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p24/r4.speaker: الله تعالى
DURR-FULL:v1p24/r4.claim: When the servant says “al-Rahman al-Rahim,” God says the servant has glorified Him.
DURR-FULL:v1p24/r4.anchor: فإذا قال {الرحمن الرحيم} يقول مجدني عبدي

DURR-FULL:v1p34/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r6.claim: Qatada says the description of creation in “Lord of the worlds” is followed by God praising Himself in “al-Rahman al-Rahim”; the Day of Judgment is when creatures are recompensed.
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله {الحمد لله رب العالمين} قال

DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.speaker: أم سلمة
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet counted the basmala as verse one, al-hamd as two, al-Rahman al-Rahim as three, Malik yawm al-din as four, then indicated five for the next verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ في الصلاة {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فعدها آية {الحمد لله رب العالمين} آيتين

DURR-FULL:v1p36/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p36/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p36/r5.claim: During a drought prayer, the Prophet invoked God as Lord of the worlds, the Merciful, and Master of Judgment, asking for rain that would sustain them; Abu Dawud calls the report rare with a good chain, and says it supports the Medinan no-alif reading.
DURR-FULL:v1p36/r5.anchor: عن عائشة قالت شكا الناس إلى رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r3.claim: The divine mercy is directed to people with needs and necessities.

TAB:1:7/r54.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r54.speaker: أهل الإلحاد الطاعنون في القرآن
TAB:1:7/r54.claim: Critics ask why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses when, they argue, the meaning of its remaining verses is already contained in “Master of Judgment Day” and “You alone we worship and ask for help.”
TAB:1:7/r54.anchor: فما الوجه إذ كان الأمر على ما وصفت في إطالة الكلام بمثل سورة أم القرآن بسبع آيات

TAB:1:7/r55.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r55.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r55.claim: Earlier scriptures each contain some meanings found together in the Qur'an: the Torah gives admonitions and detail, the Psalms praise and glorify, and the Gospel admonishes and reminds; the Qur'an gathers these and adds more.
TAB:1:7/r55.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل ، والزّبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد ، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير

TAB:1:7/r56.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r56.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r56.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the prior books lack a miracle certifying their recipients, whereas the Qur'an's unmatched composition defeats all attempts to produce even a short surah and proves Muhammad's prophethood.
TAB:1:7/r56.anchor: نظمه العجيب ، ورصفه الغريب ، وتأليفه البديع ، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء

TAB:1:7/r57.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r57.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r57.claim: The Qur'an's varied contents—encouragement, warning, commands, prohibitions, stories, argument, and parables—also make its extended expression purposeful.

TAB:1:7/r58.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r58.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r58.claim: Al-Fātiḥa's inimitable arrangement proves prophethood, while its praise and glorification direct people to recognize God's greatness, sovereignty, power, and dominion and to thank Him for His favors.
TAB:1:7/r58.anchor: ليذكروه بآلائه ويحمدوه على نعمائه ، فيستحقوا به منه المزيد ويستوجبوا عليه الثواب الجزيل

TAB:1:7/r59.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r59.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r59.claim: The account of those favored through knowledge of God and His enabling teaches that every religious and worldly blessing comes from Him, directing requests to God rather than idols or rivals.
TAB:1:7/r59.anchor: تعريف عباده أن كل ما بهم من نعمة في دينهم ودنياهم فمنه ، ليصرفوا رغبتهم إليه

TAB:1:7/r60.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r60.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r60.claim: Recounting punishments for disobedience warns people away from sin and from incurring God's anger, whose consequences lead to destruction.
TAB:1:7/r60.anchor: ترهيب عباده عن ركوب معاصيه ، والتعرض لما لا قبل لهم به من سخطه

TAB:1:7/r61.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r61.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r61.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said God answers the worshipper's recitation: He calls al-ḥamdu praise, al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm commendation, Mālik Yawm al-Dīn glorification, and the rest of the surah the servant's share.
TAB:1:7/r61.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله رب العالمين ، قال الله : حمدني عبدي

TAB:1:7/r62.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r62.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:1:7/r62.claim: A second Abū Hurayra version gives the same recitation exchange but is not attributed to the Prophet.
TAB:1:7/r62.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، قال : إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله ، فذكر نحوه ، ولم يرفعه

TAB:1:7/r63.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r63.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r63.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports the divine saying that the prayer is divided between God and His servant, with the servant receiving what he asks; the first three praises are God's, and what follows is for the servant.
TAB:1:7/r63.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين وله ما سأل

TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.speaker: بعض النصارى
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.claim: He also quotes a Christian's parody of al-Fatiha as another failed counter-imitation.

BURHAN:v3p326/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p326/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p326/r1.claim: The successive praises intensify the servant's attention: God's exclusive praise, universal lordship, gifts of mercy, and command of judgment prepare the worshipper to approach and seek help.
BURHAN:v3p326/r1.anchor: فإن العبد إذا افتتح حمد مولاه بقوله الحمد لله الدال على اختصاصه بالحمد وجد من نفسه التحرك للإقبال عليه

BURHAN:v2p475/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p475/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p475/r9.claim: Some grammarians classify juxtaposed synonymous wording without a conjunction as the same phenomenon, citing these three expressions.
BURHAN:v2p475/r9.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنه قد تجرد عن العطف

ITQAN:v4p420/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Fatiha encompasses praise, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning; every Qur’anic verse falls under one of these topics.
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.anchor: وبيان اشتمالها على علوم القرآن قرره الزمخشري باشتمالها على الثناء على الله تعالى بما هو أهله وعلى التعبد بالأمر والنهي وعلى الوعد والوعيد

ITQAN:v4p420/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.speaker: البيضاوي
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.claim: Al-Baydawi says the Fatiha contains theoretical wisdom, practical rulings in walking the straight path, and knowledge of the ranks of the blessed and abodes of the wretched.
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.anchor: وقال البيضاوي هي مشتملة على الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية التي هي سلوك الطريق المستقيم والاطلاع على مراتب السعداء ومنازل الأشقياء

ITQAN:v4p421/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.speaker: الزركشي وناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.claim: They reconcile the hadith calling the Fatiha two-thirds of the Qur’an by saying it indicates all Qur’anic aims through inclusion and implication, but not direct correspondence; those are two of three modes of indication.
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.anchor: ذكره الزركشي في شرح التنبيه وناصر الدين بن الميلق قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده

ITQAN:v4p421/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.claim: A second explanation counts three kinds of rights—God’s claim on servants, servants’ claim on God, and people’s claims on one another—and says the Fatiha explicitly covers the first two, hence two-thirds.
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.anchor: قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده وحق العباد على الله وحق بعض العباد على بعض وقد اشتملت الفاتحة صريحا على الحقين الأولين فناسب كونها بصريحها ثلثين

ITQAN:v4p421/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.claim: There is no conflict between hadiths calling the Fatiha the greatest surah and al-Baqara the greatest: al-Baqara is greatest among surahs other than the Fatiha because of its detailed laws, parables, and arguments.
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.anchor: قلت ولا تنافي أيضا بين كون الفاتحة أعظم السور وبين الحديث الآخر أن البقرة أعظم السور

ITQAN:v4p421/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi quotes a teacher saying the Fatiha contains a thousand commands, prohibitions, rulings, and reports; Ibn Umar spent eight years teaching it because of its jurisprudential depth.
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.anchor: قال ابن العربي في أحكامه سمعت بعض أشياخي يقول فيها ألف أمر وألف نهي وألف حكم وألف خبر

ITQAN:v4p490/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p490/r3.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
ITQAN:v4p490/r3.claim: Commentary on the two divine names must explain their meanings and majesty, all the divine names and attributes, and why these two are used at this point.
ITQAN:v4p490/r3.anchor: يحتاج إلى بيان الاسمين الجليلين وما يليق بهما من الجلال وما معناهما ثم يحتاج إلى بيان جميع الأسماء والصفات

ITQAN:v3p284/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.claim: The Fatiha points to all major Qur’anic disciplines: knowledge of God and attributes, prophecy, resurrection, worship, ethical conduct and the straight path, and stories teaching the outcomes of obedience and disobedience.
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.anchor: وقد وجه ذلك بأن العلوم التي احتوى عليها القرآن قامت بها الأديان أربعة علم الأصول ومداره على معرفة الله وصفاته

ITQAN:v3p284/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.claim: By signaling all Qur’anic aims, the Fatiha achieves an exemplary opening and combines beautiful words, pleasing cadence, and rhetorical forms.
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.anchor: فنبه في الفاتحة على جميع مقاصد القرآن وهذا هو الغاية في براعة الاستهلال مع ما اشتملت عليه من الألفاظ الحسنة والمقاطع المستحسنة وأنواع البلاغة

ITQAN:v2p543#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p543#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p543#2/r3.claim: Al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is read with all three case endings.

ITQAN:v3p269/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p269/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p269/r9.claim: The less emphatic description may follow the more emphatic one; raʾfa is more intense than mercy, explaining the sequence raʾuf then rahim.
ITQAN:v3p269/r9.anchor: تأخير الوصف غير الأبلغ عن الأبلغ ومنه ﴿ الرحمن الرحيم ﴾ ﴿ رؤوف رحيم ﴾ لأن الرأفة أبلغ من الرحمة

RUMMANI:v1p97/r9.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r9.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r9.claim: Nearby letters include mīm with nūn in al-Fātiḥa and dāl with bāʾ in the quoted Qur'anic phrase endings.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r9.anchor: وأما الحروف المتقاربة فكالميم من النون , كقوله تعالى: {الرحمن الرحيم مالك يوم الدين} , وكالدال مع الباء نحو: {ف والقرآن المجيد} ثم فال: {هذا شيء عجيب}

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#4/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#4/r10.claim: Faʿlān conveys a renewed or changing quality, whereas faʿīl conveys a stable one; Rahmān and Rahīm together affirm that God’s mercy is both permanent and continually renewed.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#4/r10.anchor: فإن صيغة (فعلان) تفيد الحدوث والتجدد، وصيغة (فعيل) تفيد الثبوت

NASHR:v1p227/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p227/r4.claim: Stopping after these phrases is good because their sense is understood, but starting with attached phrases such as rabb al-ʿālamīn, ṣirāṭ alladhīna, or ghayr al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim is poor, except at verse ends per the Sunnah.
NASHR:v1p227/r4.anchor: الوقف على ذلك وما أشبهه حسن ; لأن المراد من ذلك يفهم، ولكن الابتداء ب (الرحمن الرحيم

NASHR:v1p49/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r7.speaker: قتيبة عن الكسائي، كردم عن نافع، ورش
NASHR:v1p49/r7.claim: The author adds unlisted transmissions: Qutayba from al-Kisa'i has imāla in al-ʿālamīn and al-raḥmān; Kurram from Nafi and al-Ahwazi from Warsh lengthen vowels in mālik, naʿbudu, and iyyāka.
NASHR:v1p49/r7.anchor: وبقي منها روايات أخرى رويناها منها إمالة (العالمين والرحمن) بخلاف لقتيبة عن الكسائي، ومنها إشباع الكسرة من (ملك يوم الدين)

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r1.claim: Raḥmān and raḥīm, already discussed in the basmala, and rabb al-ʿālamīn are praise epithets following the unique divine name.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r1.anchor: { الرحمن الرحيم } تقدم الكلام عليهما في البسملة

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r2.claim: The sequence begins with lordship; when rabb means master, owner, or deity, God's control makes mercy the fitting next description, sustaining hope of pardon after error.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r2.anchor: وبدأ أولا بالوصف بالربوبية ،   فإن كان الرب بمعنى السيد ،   أو بمعنى المالك

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r3.claim: Rabb cannot mean “the constant one” or “companion,” because neither sense can be annexed to al-ʿālamīn; if it means “reformer,” mercy implies little need for reform, since compassion motivates reform.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r3.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون الرب بمعى الثابت ،   ولا بمعنى الصاحب

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r4.claim: Whoever is characterized by lordship and mercy toward those under His care is deserving of praise.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r4.anchor: إن من كان موصوفا بالربوبية والرحمة للمربوبين كان مستحقا للحمد

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r5.claim: The majority read the two epithets in the genitive as adjectives; apposition and explanatory apposition are also proposed parses.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r5.anchor: وخفض الرحمن الرحيم الجمهور ،   ونصبهما أبو العالية

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r6.speaker: أبو العالية وابن السميفع وعيسى بن عمرو
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya, Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿAmr read raḥmān and raḥīm in the accusative as detached praise.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r6.anchor: ونصبهما أبو العالية وابن السميفع وعيسى بن عمرو

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r7.speaker: أبو رزين العقيلي والربيع بن خيثم وأبو عمران الجوني
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r7.claim: Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī, al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, and Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī read the epithets in the nominative, also as detached praise.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r7.anchor: ورفعهما أبو رزين العقيلي والربيع بن خيثم وأبو عمران الجوني

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r8.claim: The genitive can be adjectival, appositional, or explanatory; nominative and accusative readings detach the words from the preceding construction.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r8.anchor: فالخفض على النعت ،   وقيل في الخفض إنه بدل أو عطف بيان

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r9.claim: If the basmala is part of al-Fātiḥa, repeating raḥmān and raḥīm underscores the greatness of these attributes and reinforces them.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r9.anchor: وفي تكرار الرحمن الرحيم إن كانت التسمية آية من الفاتحة

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r10.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r10.claim: Makkī argues that repetition proves the basmala is not a verse of al-Fātiḥa: adjacent verses of the same meaning do not occur without a separating cadence, and he says al-ḥamdu does not really separate them.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r10.anchor: وجعل مكي تكرارها دليلا على أن التسمية ليست بآية من الفاتحة

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r11.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r11.claim: Makkī proposes reading the sequence as “praise belongs to God, the Merciful, the Compassionate, Lord of the worlds,” placing mercy beside praise and kingship beside kingship.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r11.anchor: تقديره الحمد لله ،   الرحمن الرحيم ،   رب العالمين

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r12.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls Makkī's argument defective and defends the Qur'anic order: lordship and mercy precede dominion on Judgment Day and worship, pairing lordship with dominion and mercy with worship.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r12.anchor: والترتيب القرآني جاء في غاية الفصاحة لأنه تعالى وصف نفسه بصفة الربوبية

ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r13.claim: Exegetes classify pauses as complete, sufficient, improper, and other kinds, with books arranged by sūra; Abū Ḥayyān says knowledge of Arabic makes these manuals unnecessary.
ABUHAYYAN:1:3/r13.anchor: وقد ذكر المفسرون في علم التفسير الوقف ،   وقد اختلف في أقسامه

ALUSI:1:3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:3/r1.claim: After describing God’s universal lordship, al-Ālūsī says these names explicitly declare the greatness of His mercy.
ALUSI:1:3/r1.anchor: بعدما ذكر سبحانه وتعالى عموم تربيته صرح بعظيم رحمته فقال عز شأنه

ALUSI:1:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:3/r2.claim: Most readers put both names in the genitive; Zayd, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Ibn al-Sumayqa, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿAmr read them accusatively; Abū Razīn, al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, and Abū ʿImrān read them nominatively.
ALUSI:1:3/r2.anchor: والجمهور على خفضهما ، ونصبهما زيد وأبو العالية وابن السميقع وعيسى بن عمور ، ورفعهما أبو رزين العقيلي والربيع بن خيثم وأبو عمران الجولي

ALUSI:1:3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r3.speaker: بعض ساداتنا
ALUSI:1:3/r3.claim: Some of al-Ālūsī’s learned predecessors infer from repeating these names that the basmala is not a verse of al-Fātiḥa.
ALUSI:1:3/r3.anchor: واستدل بعض ساداتنا بتكرارهما على أن البسملة ليست آية من الفاتحة

ALUSI:1:3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:3/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls that inference weak: the names in the basmala explain beginning in God’s name, while their repetition here explains why He merits praise.
ALUSI:1:3/r4.anchor: وليس بالقوي لأن التكرار لفائدة ، فذكرهما في البسملة تعليل للابتداء باسمه عز شأنه

ALUSI:1:3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r5.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI:1:3/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī says mercy is repeated to show that divine concern for mercy exceeds concern for other matters; mention of the Day of Judgment then prevents complacency, as in 40:3.
ALUSI:1:3/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام الرازي قدس سره في بيان حكمة التكرار : التقدير كأنه قيل له اذكر أني إله ورب مرة واحدة واذكر أني

ALUSI:1:3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:3/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī has a reservation about al-Rāzī’s account because divinity, too, is repeated in the passage.
ALUSI:1:3/r6.anchor: فإن الألوهية مكررة أيضاً كما ترى

ALUSI:1:3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:3/r7.claim: In al-Ālūsī’s Sufi account, these names unpack the otherwise general lordship: nurturing may be direct or mediated, and mediated care may involve hardship or ease.
ALUSI:1:3/r7.anchor: وعندي بمسلك صوفي أن ذكر الرحمن الرحيم تفصيل من وجه لما في رب العالمين من الإجمال

ALUSI:1:3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:3/r8.claim: Al-Raḥmān signals God’s nurturing through intermediaries and otherwise throughout His realm; this mercy may be mixed with painful but beneficial hardship, like bitter medicine.
ALUSI:1:3/r8.anchor: فالرحمن يشير إلى التربية بالوسائط وغيرها في عالمه

ALUSI:1:3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:3/r9.claim: Al-Raḥīm signals nurturing without intermediary in His words; its mercy is pure favor, unmixed with pain, and belongs to those of complete felicity.
ALUSI:1:3/r9.anchor: ورحمة الرحيم لا يمازجها شوب فهي محض النعم ، ولا توجد إلا عند أهل السعادات الكاملة

BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.claim: In a qudsi report, God divides prayer between Himself and His servant and answers each part of al-Fatiha; Baghawi grades it sahih.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.anchor: قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ، نصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل ،

BAYDAWI:1:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:3/r1.claim: The repeated “al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm” supplies a causal explanation, which Bayḍāwī will discuss below.

BIQAI:1:3/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:3/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:3/r1.claim: Lordship is not fully sound without mercy, so al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm follow to encourage continued praise; together they detail twice over what al-ḥamd originally encompassed.
BIQAI:1:3/r1.anchor: ولما كانت مرتبة الربوبية لا تستجمع الصلاح إلا بالرحمة

BIQAI:1:3/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:3/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:3/r2.claim: Biqāʿī says he will explain the secret of repeating these attributes at 6:118 by Imam al-Ghazālī's principle that the Qur'an contains no repetition.
BIQAI:1:3/r2.anchor: عن الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي رحمه الله تعالى{[170]} أنه لا مكرر في القرآن

BIQAI:1:3/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:3/r3.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI:1:3/r3.claim: Al-Ghazālī's interpretive principle, invoked for the repeated attributes, is that nothing in the Qur'an is redundant repetition.
BIQAI:1:3/r3.anchor: عن الإمام حجة الإسلام الغزالي رحمه الله تعالى{[170]} أنه لا مكرر في القرآن

DURR:1:1/r114.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:1/r114.speaker: الله
DURR:1:1/r114.claim: The report says reciting the two mercy names magnifies God.
DURR:1:1/r114.anchor: فإذا قال { الرحمن الرحيم } يقول مجدني عبدي .

DURR:1:3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:3/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR:1:3/r2.claim: Qatada says the Compassionate, the Merciful is God praising Himself.
DURR:1:3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله { الحمد لله رب العالمين } قال : ما وصف من خلقه . وفي قوله { الرحمن الرحيم } قال : مدح نفسه

DURR:1:3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:3/r4.speaker: رسول الله
DURR:1:3/r4.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited the basmala in prayer and counted it as verse one, al-hamd as verse two, al-Rahman al-Rahim as verse three, Malik Yawm al-Din as verse four, and joined the worship-prayer as verse five with his fingers.
DURR:1:3/r4.anchor: عن أم سلمة " أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ في الصلاة { بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم } فعدها آية { الحمد لله رب العالمين } آيتين

ABUDAWUD:821/r2.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.claim: In a hadith qudsi transmitted by Abu Hurayra, God divides al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise and glorification receive divine responses, worship is mutual, and the guidance petition belongs to the servant.
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.anchor: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى قَسَمْتُ الصَّلاَةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي

IBNASHUR:1:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r1.claim: Al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm are both derived from the root r-ḥ-m.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r1.anchor: وصفان مشتقان من رحم ، وفي « تفسير القرطبي »

IBNASHUR:1:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r2.speaker: المبرد
IBNASHUR:1:3/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad, cited by Ibn al-Anbārī through al-Qurṭubī, says al-Raḥmān is a Hebrew name borrowed into Arabic and originally had khāʾ.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r2.anchor: عن ابن الأَنباري عن المبرد أن الرحمن اسم عبراني نقل إلى العربية قال وأصله بالخاء المعجمة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r3.speaker: جرير
IBNASHUR:1:3/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad adduces Jarīr’s line to al-Akhṭal, in the khāʾ reading, as evidence for the form رَخْمان.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r3.anchor: وأنشد على ذلك قول جرير يخاطب الأخطل

IBNASHUR:1:3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says al-Mubarrad offers no proof; Arabic and Hebrew are sister languages, and Arabic may be older, so al-Raḥmān could be Arabic.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r4.anchor: ولم يأت المبرد بحجة على ما زعمه ، ولم لا يكون الرحمن عربيا كما كان عبرانيا فإن العربية والعبرانية أختان

IBNASHUR:1:3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r5.claim: The polytheists’ question “What is al-Raḥmān?” (25:60) may have prompted the claim that Arabs did not know this divine name.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r5.anchor: ولعل الذي جرأه على ادعاء أن الرحمن اسم عبراني

IBNASHUR:1:3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r6.claim: Some Arabs in Yemen say رَخِم or رَخْمَة with khāʾ, which bears on the proposed Arabic or Hebrew etymology.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r6.anchor: كما سيأتي بعض عرب اليمن يقولون رخم رخمة بالمعجمة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r7.claim: In Arabic, mercy is a tender inward feeling and inclination toward a living being that prompts gentleness, beneficence, harm prevention, and help through hardship.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r7.anchor: واسم الرحمة موضوع في اللغة العربية لرقة الخاطر وانعطافه نحو حي بحيث تحمل من اتصف بها على الرفق بالمرحوم

IBNASHUR:1:3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r8.claim: As a psychological quality, mercy is a passive affect; its effects are active deeds prompted by that affect and limited by the person’s capacity.
