IBNASHUR:1:3/r8.anchor: فهي من الكيفيات النفسانية لأنها انفعال ، ولتلك الكيفية اندفاع يحمل صاحبها على أفعال وجودية

IBNASHUR:1:3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r9.claim: Calling someone merciful describes an inward affect, while saying that they have mercy on someone means that effects of mercy issue from them; the transitive verb names those effects.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r9.anchor: فأصل الرحمة من مقولة الانفعال وآثارها من مقولة الفعل ، فإذا وصف موصوف بالرحمة كان معناه حصول الانفعال

IBNASHUR:1:3/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r10.claim: Mercy’s essence has no discrete external instances; what has instances are its effects.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r10.anchor: فليس لماهية الرحمة جزئيات وجودية ولكنها جزئيات من آثارها

IBNASHUR:1:3/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r11.claim: Languages describe God with mercy according to what their communities believe can or cannot be attributed to God; most earlier nations were anthropomorphists.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r11.anchor: فوصف الله تعالى بصفات الرحمة في اللغات ناشىء على مقدار عقائد أهلها فيما يجوز على الله ويستحيل

IBNASHUR:1:3/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r12.claim: Scriptural language expresses elevated meanings as far as ordinary language allows, while believers affirm God’s transcendence from created accidents, as in 42:11.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r12.anchor: مع اعتقاد تنزيه الله عن أعراض المخلوقات بالدليل العام على التنزيه

IBNASHUR:1:3/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r13.claim: Believers do not understand divine mercy as the human emotional affect; for God it means the intended goal of mercy, the issuance of gentleness, kindness, beneficence, and aid.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r13.anchor: فأهل الإيمان إذا سمعوا أو أطلقوا وصفي الرحمن الرحيم لا يفهمون منه حصول ذلك الانفعال الملحوظ في حقيقة الرحمة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r14.claim: The human limitations normally included in mercy’s meaning matter only insofar as they enable mercy’s effects in people.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r14.anchor: لأن ما عدا ذلك من القيود الملحوظة في مسمى الرحمة في متعارف الناس لا أهمية له لولا أنه لا يمكن بدونه حصول آثاره فيهم

IBNASHUR:1:3/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r15.claim: A person may pity someone yet be unable to benefit them because of incapacity, showing that an inner feeling and its effective outcome differ.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r15.anchor: ألا ترى أن المرء قد يرحم أحدا ولا يملك له نفعا لعجز أو نحوه

IBNASHUR:1:3/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r16.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
IBNASHUR:1:3/r16.claim: Al-Ghazālī says a capable person who wants to meet a need but does not do so is not merciful; an incapable person may be called merciful for the pity felt, but that mercy is incomplete.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r16.anchor: وقد أشار إلى ما قلناه أبو حامد الغزالي

IBNASHUR:1:3/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r17.claim: These divine attributes are not ambiguous in the relevant sense: frequent use makes the intended meaning readily apparent, and reason establishes that God lacks unbefitting implications, as with knowledge, life, and power.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r17.anchor: ليس من المتشابه لتبادر المعنى المراد منه بكثرة استعماله وتحقق تنزه الله عن لوازم المعنى المقصود في الوضع مما لا يليق بجلال الله

IBNASHUR:1:3/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r18.claim: Scripture has transferred divine mercy to mean God’s willing to convey beneficence to creatures in worldly life; 7:156 affirms this mercy, and most beautiful names are transferred similarly.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r18.anchor: فوصفه تعالى بالرحمن الرحيم من المنقولات الشرعية فقد أثبت القرآن رحمة الله

IBNASHUR:1:3/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r19.claim: The mutashābih is what points more strongly toward a meaning that cannot properly be attributed to God; Ibn ʿĀshūr refers to 3:7 for this category.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r19.anchor: وأما المتشابه فهو ما كانت دلالته على المعنى المنزه عنه أقوى وأشد

IBNASHUR:1:3/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r20.speaker: صاحب الكشاف وكثير من المحققين
IBNASHUR:1:3/r20.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s Kashshāf and many exacting scholars take al-Raḥmān as a ṣifa mushabbaha, like ghaḍbān.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r20.anchor: والذي ذهب إليه صاحب الكشاف } وكثير من المحققين

IBNASHUR:1:3/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r21.claim: Although ṣifa mushabbaha is normally formed from an intransitive verb, a transitive verb can become an innate disposition and be treated like an instinctive verb, with its middle vowel changed to ḍamma.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r21.anchor: والصفة المشبهة إنما تصاغ من فعل لازم إلا أن الفعل المتعدي إذا صار كالسجية لموصوفه ينزل منزلة أفعال الغرائز

IBNASHUR:1:3/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r22.claim: This conversion is recognized either by hearing the converted verb, as in faquha, or by its resulting adjective when the verb is rarely heard, as with balīgh; al-Raḥmān is analogous though raḥuma is unattested.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r22.anchor: وإنما يعرف هذا التحويل بأحد أمرين إما بسماع الفعل المحول مثل فقه وإما بوجود أثره وهو الصفة المشبهة مثل بليغ

IBNASHUR:1:3/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r23.speaker: ابن مالك
IBNASHUR:1:3/r23.claim: Some grammarians, including Ibn Mālik in his Sharḥ al-Tashīl, deny that al-Raḥmān is a ṣifa mushabbaha because its source verb is transitive; he compares it with rabb and malik.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r23.anchor: ومن النحاة من منع أن يكون الرحمن صفة مشبهة بناء على أن الفعل المشتق هو منه فعل متعد وإليه مال ابن مالك

IBNASHUR:1:3/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r24.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR:1:3/r24.claim: Sībawayh treats al-Raḥīm as an intensive form that retains the verb’s transitive meaning.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r24.anchor: وأما الرحيم فذهب سيبويه إلى أنه من أمثلة المبالغة وهو باق على دلالته على التعدي

IBNASHUR:1:3/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r25.speaker: صاحب الكشاف والجمهور
IBNASHUR:1:3/r25.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and the majority do not recognize faʿīl as an intensive pattern, so they classify al-Raḥīm as a ṣifa mushabbaha like marīḍ and saqīm.

IBNASHUR:1:3/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r26.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r26.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers Sībawayh’s analysis of al-Raḥīm as an intensive form.

IBNASHUR:1:3/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r27.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r27.claim: Linguists agree that both attributes intensify mercy, conveying its firmness and its relation to many recipients; they differ on how the intensity is expressed and whether the terms are synonymous.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r27.anchor: ولا خلاف بين أهل اللغة في أن الوصفين دالان على المبالغة في صفة الرحمة أي تمكنها وتعلقها بكثير من المرحومين وإنما الخلاف

IBNASHUR:1:3/r28.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r28.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r28.claim: The intensified sense is established by usage, which generally follows the linguistic principle that greater form signals greater meaning.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r28.anchor: والحق أن استفادة المبالغة حاصلة من تتبع الاستعمال وأن الاستعمال جرى على نكتة في مراعاة واضعي اللغة زيادة المبنى لقصد زيادة في معنى المادة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r29.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r29.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR:1:3/r29.claim: The Kashshāf states the common principle that an increase in a word’s construction signals an increase in meaning.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r29.anchor: قال في « الكشاف » : « ويقولون إن الزيادة في البناء لزيادة المعنى

IBNASHUR:1:3/r30.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r30.speaker: الزجاج
IBNASHUR:1:3/r30.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains ghaḍbān as one filled with anger, illustrating the intensive force of the form.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r30.anchor: وقال الزجاج في الغضبان هو الممتلىء غضبا

IBNASHUR:1:3/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r31.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR:1:3/r31.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī recounts an Arab naming a light conveyance shiqindāf instead of shaqandaf, adding to the word’s form to mark a greater referent.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r31.anchor: ومما طن على أذني من ملح العرب أنهم يسمون مركبا من مراكبهم بالشقدف وهو مركب خفيف

IBNASHUR:1:3/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r32.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r32.claim: The form-size principle is predominant rather than exceptionless; some additions add a new meaning instead of intensifying the root.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r32.anchor: وهي قاعدة أغلبية لا تتخلف إلا في زيادات معروفة موضوعة لزيادة معنى جديد دون زيادة في أصل معنى المادة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r33.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r33.claim: The diminutive yāʾ adds a distinct meaning to the base rather than increasing the root’s original meaning.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r33.anchor: مثل زيادة ياء التصغير فقد أفادت معنى زائدا على أصل المادة وليس زيادة في معنى المادة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r34.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r34.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r34.claim: Ḥadhir is an intensive form with fewer letters than ḥādhir, another exception to the form-size rule.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r34.anchor: وأما نحو حذر الذي هو من أمثلة المبالغة وهو أقل حروفا من حاذر

IBNASHUR:1:3/r35.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r35.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن جني والزجاج والزمخشري
IBNASHUR:1:3/r35.claim: Most scholars, including Abū ʿUbayda, Ibn Jinnī, al-Zajjāj, and al-Zamakhsharī, hold that al-Raḥmān is more intensive than al-Raḥīm because its form is longer.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r35.anchor: وإلى ذلك مال جمهور المحققين مثل أبي عبيدة وابن جني والزجاج والزمخشري وعلى رعي هذه القاعدة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r36.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r36.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r36.claim: This ranking raises a rhetorical problem: why append al-Raḥīm after al-Raḥmān when eloquence normally progresses from general to specific and from strong to stronger?
IBNASHUR:1:3/r36.anchor: فقد شاع ورود إشكال على وجه إرداف وصفه الرحمن بوصفه بالرحيم مع أن شأن أهل البلاغة إذا أجروا وصفين في معنى واحد

IBNASHUR:1:3/r37.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r37.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r37.claim: Most exegetes resolve the sequence by treating al-Raḥmān as more specific, so al-Raḥīm broadens the scope after a restricted description; al-Raḥmān is exclusive to God.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r37.anchor: مرجعها إلى اعتبار الرحمن أخص من الرحيم فتعقيب الأول بالثاني تعميم بعد خاص ولذلك كان وصف الرحمن مختصا به تعالى

IBNASHUR:1:3/r38.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r38.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r38.claim: Al-Raḥīm signifies mercy with many objects, so it can describe someone other than God, as 9:128 calls the Messenger raʾūf and raḥīm; the two attributes are not redundant.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r38.anchor: ومدلول الرحيم كون الرحمة كثيرة التعلق إذ هو من أمثلة المبالغة ولذلك كان يطلق على غير الله تعالى كما في قوله تعالى في حق رسوله

IBNASHUR:1:3/r39.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r39.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r39.claim: Al-Raḥmān precedes al-Raḥīm because an attribute of essential character comes before one indicating the many recipients of that attribute.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r39.anchor: وتقديم الرحمن على الرحيم لأن الصيغة الدالة على الاتصاف الذاتي أولى بالتقديم في التوصيف من الصفة الدالة على كثرة متعلقاتها

IBNASHUR:1:3/r40.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r40.speaker: قطرب
IBNASHUR:1:3/r40.claim: Quṭrub says al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm are equivalent ṣifa mushabbaha forms and that their pairing is verbal emphasis; al-Zajjāj leaned toward this view.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r40.anchor: وينسب إلى قطرب أن الرحمن والرحيم يدلان على معنى واحد

IBNASHUR:1:3/r41.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r41.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r41.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects Quṭrub’s emphasis analysis as weak: emphasis is contrary to the default preference for adding a new meaning, and the context does not call for emphasis; other proposed solutions also fail to persuade.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r41.anchor: وهو وجه ضعيف إذ التوكيد خلاف الأصل والتأسيس خير من التأكيد

IBNASHUR:1:3/r42.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r42.speaker: جمهور الأئمة
IBNASHUR:1:3/r42.claim: The majority of leading scholars say al-Raḥmān was not used in pre-Islamic Arabic; the Qur’an introduced it as God’s attribute, so it became exclusive to Him, and some call it a proper name rather than an adjective.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r42.anchor: وقد ذكر جمهور الأئمة أن وصف الرحمن لم يطلق في كلام العرب قبل الإسلام وأن القرآن هو الذي جاء به صفة لله تعالى فلذلك اختص به تعالى حتى قيل إنه اسم له وليس بصفة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r43.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r43.speaker: جمهور الأئمة
IBNASHUR:1:3/r43.claim: The Qur’an’s report that people asked “What is al-Raḥmān?” and said they disbelieved in Him (25:60; 13:30) supports the claim that the name was unknown or rejected.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r43.anchor: واستدلوا على ذلك بقوله تعالى : { وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن }

IBNASHUR:1:3/r44.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r44.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r44.claim: These objections recur especially in Makkan sūras such as al-Furqān and al-Mulk; al-Mulk repeats the name or its pronoun eight times, emphasizing its establishment as a divine name.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r44.anchor: وقد تكرر مثل هاتين الآيتين في القرآن وخاصة في السور المكية مثل سورة الفرقان وسورة الملك وقد ذكر الرحمن في سورة الملك باسمه الظاهر وضميره ثماني مرات

IBNASHUR:1:3/r45.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r45.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r45.claim: The evidence suggests the epithet had fallen out of common use, or that people denied it as a name of God.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r45.anchor: فالظاهر أن هذا الوصف تنوسي في كلامهم ، أو أنكروا أن يكون من أسماء الله

IBNASHUR:1:3/r46.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r46.speaker: بعض شعراء بني حنيفة
IBNASHUR:1:3/r46.claim: A Banū Ḥanīfa poet called Musaylima raḥmānan after Islam, during the Yamāma apostasy, when his followers styled him “Raḥmān of Yamāma” in an act of extreme disbelief.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r46.anchor: وأما قول بعض شعراء بني حنيفة في مسيلمة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r47.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r47.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r47.claim: The Qur’an says “al-Raḥmān” in the Makkan 67:19 but “Allah” in 16:79, a portion revealed in Medina, underscoring the Makkan effort to establish this divine name.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r47.anchor: ومن دقائق القرآن أنه آثر اسم الرحمن

IBNASHUR:1:3/r48.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r48.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r48.claim: Following “Lord of the worlds” (1:2) with these names is apt: God governs and brings worlds to bodily and spiritual perfection, while weak creatures naturally need and hope for mercy.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r48.anchor: وإجراء هذين الوصفين العليين على اسم الجلالة بعد وصفه بأنه رب العالمين لمناسبة ظاهرة للبليغ لأنه بعد أن وصف بما هو مقتضى استحقاقه الحمد

IBNASHUR:1:3/r49.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r49.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r49.claim: Al-Raḥmān names mercy as God’s intrinsic attribute whose effects issue universally and consistently; this especially suits Him as Lord of weak creatures.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r49.anchor: ناسب أن يتبع ذلك بوصفه بالرحمن أي الذي الرحمة له وصف ذاتي تصدر عنه آثاره بعموم واطراد على ما تقدم

IBNASHUR:1:3/r50.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r50.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r50.claim: Although lordship entails gradual growth to perfection and all blessings, al-Raḥmān clarifies that this care reaches perfection gently, in ways suited to each creature’s capacity.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r50.anchor: قلت لأن الرحمة تتضمن أن ذلك الإبلاغ إلى الكمال لم يكن على وجه الإعنات بل كان برعاية ما يناسب كل نوع وفرد ويلائم طوقه واستعداده

IBNASHUR:1:3/r51.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r51.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r51.claim: Lordly blessings may involve hardship or pain; al-Raḥmān signals that they arrive through gentleness, ease, and removal of hardship, including in religious commands so far as their purpose allows.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r51.anchor: والنعمة قد تحصل بضرب من الشدة والأذى

IBNASHUR:1:3/r52.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r52.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r52.claim: Some of God’s governance mercies are obvious: He enables people to live on earth and makes its benefits accessible.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r52.anchor: فمعظم تدبيره تعالى بنا هو رحمات ظاهرة كالتمكين من الأرض وتيسير منافعها

IBNASHUR:1:3/r53.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r53.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r53.claim: Other mercies appear in duties that serve people, such as purification and the cultivation of good character, with ease observed as far as possible.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r53.anchor: ومنه ما رحمته بمراعاة اليسر بقدر الإمكان مثل التكاليف الراجعة إلى منافعنا كالطهارة وبث مكارم الأخلاق

IBNASHUR:1:3/r54.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r54.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r54.claim: Some duties benefit the public; mercy for the community extends to everyone through social order, as in zakāt.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r54.anchor: ومنها ما منفعته للجمهور فتتبعها رحمات الجميع لأن في رحمة الجمهور رحمة بالبقية في انتظام الأحوال كالزكاة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r55.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r55.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:3/r55.claim: Grammarians disagree whether bare (indefinite) raḥmān declines or is diptote; the Kāfiya gives two criteria for diptote faʿlān adjectives, yielding a dispute over this form.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r55.anchor: قال في « الكافية » : « النون والألف إذا كانا في صفة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r56.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r56.speaker: بنو أسد
IBNASHUR:1:3/r56.claim: Banū Asad decline every faʿlān adjective because they give each a feminine form in faʿlānah.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r56.anchor: وبنو أسد يصرفون جميع فعلان لأنهم يقولون في كل مؤنث له فعلانة

IBNASHUR:1:3/r57.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:3/r57.speaker: الزمخشري والرضى وابن مالك
IBNASHUR:1:3/r57.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Raḍī, and Ibn Mālik choose to treat raḥmān as diptote.
IBNASHUR:1:3/r57.anchor: واختار الزمخشري والرضى وابن مالك عدم صرفه

NASAFI:1:1/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:1/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
NASAFI:1:1/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God’s dialogue dividing the Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise, glorification, and exaltation belong to God; the worshipper’s request for guidance and the response to it belong to the servant, while worship and aid are shared.
NASAFI:1:1/r12.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة أي الفاتحة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ولعبدي ما سأل

NASAFI:1:3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:3/r1.claim: The names al-Rahman and al-Rahim were already mentioned in the basmala; repeating them here would add no information if the basmala were part of the Fatiha, so the repetition indicates it is not.
NASAFI:1:3/r1.anchor: ذكرهما قد مر وهو دليل على أن التسمية ليست من الفاتحة

QURTUBI:1:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:3/r1.claim: After Rabb al-ʿālamīn evokes awe and fear, God names Himself the All-Merciful and Merciful to inspire hope; joining fear and hope better assists obedience and restrains disobedience.
QURTUBI:1:3/r1.anchor: لأنه لما كان في اتصافه ب " رب العالمين " ترهيب قرنه ب " الرحمن الرحيم " لما تضمن من الترغيب

QURTUBI:1:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:3/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:1:3/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports in Muslim that if a believer knew God’s punishment, no one would hope for Paradise, and if a disbeliever knew His mercy, no one would despair of Paradise.
QURTUBI:1:3/r2.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( لو يعلم المؤمن ما عند الله من العقوبة

RAZI:1:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r1.claim: Razi sketches the sūra’s sequence: seek refuge from sins, begin good works in God’s name, praise and recognize his lordship and mercy, heed judgment, worship and seek help, ask guidance, and avoid ignorance and error.
RAZI:1:1/r1.anchor: بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم } نشرع في أداء كل الخيرات والمأمورات

RAZI:1:3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:3/r1.claim: Mercy means both rescuing people from kinds of affliction and bringing benefits to those in need.
RAZI:1:3/r1.anchor: أن الرحمة عبارة عن التخليص من أنواع الآفات

RAZI:1:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:1:3/r2.claim: Knowing how God rescues people requires knowing the many afflictions; medical works reveal only some possible diseases in each organ and body part.
RAZI:1:3/r2.anchor: لا يمكن معرفته إلا بعد معرفة أقسام الآفات ،   وهي كثيرة لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى

RAZI:1:3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:1:3/r3.claim: Reflection on how God guided human minds to identify foods and medicines from minerals, plants and animals opens an ocean of knowledge without shore.
RAZI:1:3/r3.anchor: كيف هدى عقول الخلق إلى معرفة أقسام الأغذية والأدوية من المعادن والنبات والحيوان

RAZI:1:3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:3/r4.speaker: جالينوس
RAZI:1:3/r4.claim: Razi recounts Galen’s story that, while writing about the eye’s benefits, he withheld his account of the divine wisdom in the two hollow optic nerves meeting at one place; an angel in a dream rebuked him, so he wrote the account.
RAZI:1:3/r4.anchor: حكى جالينوس أنه لما صنف كتابه في منافع أعضاء العين قال : بخلت على الناس بذكر حكمة الله تعالى

RAZI:1:3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:3/r5.speaker: جالينوس
RAZI:1:3/r5.claim: Galen said his thickened spleen resisted every treatment he knew; in a vision an angel directed him to bleed the vein between the little and ring fingers, which cured it.
RAZI:1:3/r5.anchor: إن طحالي قد غلظ فعالجته بكل ما عرفت فلم ينفع

RAZI:1:3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:1:3/r6.claim: Razi says many early medical signs trace to promptings and inspirations like Galen’s experiences, and reflection on them shows that divine mercy exceeds measurement and enumeration.
RAZI:1:3/r6.anchor: أكثر علامات الطب في أوائلها تنتهي إلى أمثال هذه التنبيهات والإلهامات

ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r1.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains the divine attributes as meaning ‘possessor of mercy.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r1.anchor: معناه فيما ذكر أبو عبيدة: ذو الرحمة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r2.claim: The pattern faʿlān intensifies a quality, as ‘ghaḍbān’ means filled with anger; ‘raḥmān’ describes mercy encompassing everything and is reserved for God.
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r2.anchor: وإنما كان ذلك لأن بناء فعلان من أبنية ما يبالغ في وصفه، ألا ترى أنك إذا قلت غضبان فمعناه الممتلئ غضبا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r3.claim: Because God's mercy encompasses everything, ‘al-Raḥmān’ may not be used of anyone besides God.
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r3.anchor: فرحمن الذي وسعت رحمته كل شي فلا يجوز أن يقال لغير الله رحمن.

ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r4.claim: The two attributes are genitive because they praise God and follow the grammatical case of His name.
ZAJJAJ:v1p43/r4.anchor: وخفضت هذه الصفات لأنها ثناء على الله - عز وجل - فكان إعرابها إعراب اسمه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r4.claim: Biqāʿī associates al-Raḥmān with lordship in the first and second creations, and al-Raḥīm especially with the second creation, preservation, recompense, and special mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r4.anchor: وهي أن الرحمن مشير غلى ما قال من جهة الربوبية
